code_decode.name: code_decode
code_decode.title: Decode an instruction
code_decode.description: Decode one target instruction through CheatEngine.Client and return Cheat Engine's columns, exact bytes and exact length. Use code_disassemble when surrounding instructions are needed.

address.description: An instruction address or Cheat Engine expression.
The instruction address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

opcode.description: The mnemonic and operands as Cheat Engine displayed them.

extra.description: Cheat Engine's annotation column; empty when there is none.

text.description: Opcode and annotation as one display line.

bytes.description: The exact target bytes decoded, uppercase hexadecimal without separators.

length.description: Cheat Engine's exact instruction length, repeated for callers that only need the size.

code_disassemble.name: code_disassemble
code_disassemble.title: Disassemble code
code_disassemble.description: Disassemble 1 to 1024 target instructions with CheatEngine.Client's typed instruction API. before asks Cheat Engine for estimated predecessor boundaries, so it is useful for context but cannot prove a variable-length instruction boundary. The returned bytes are read from target memory in the same Client operation.

address.description: An instruction address or Cheat Engine expression, such as game.exe+1C0.

count.description: The number of forward instructions, 1 to 1024 after any predecessors.

before.description: The estimated predecessor instructions to include, 0 to 1024; count plus before is at most 1024.

address.description: The resolved address supplied by the caller, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

instructions.description: The instructions, from the earliest requested predecessor through the final instruction.

address.description: The instruction address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

opcode.description: The mnemonic and operands as Cheat Engine displayed them.

extra.description: Cheat Engine's annotation column; empty when there is none.

text.description: Opcode and annotation as one display line.

bytes.description: The exact target bytes decoded, uppercase hexadecimal without separators.

debugger_attach.name: debugger_attach
debugger_attach.title: Attach debugger
debugger_attach.description: Attaches Cheat Engine's debugger to the selected local process. Windows is the compatible interface; VEH injects a helper and requires target_code_execution, and kernel requires kernel_access. default attaches the interface selected in Cheat Engine's settings: MCP reads that setting first and refuses with unsupported when it selects the DBVM debugger or cannot be identified, and with capability_disabled when the selected interface needs a switch that is off (VEH needs target_code_execution, kernel needs kernel_access); an already attached debugger is only reported. While Cheat Engine is connected to a ceserver, an attach is refused with unsupported before Cheat Engine attaches its network debugger, and an attached interface MCP cannot drive, such as DBVM, a GDB server or ceserver, is reported as unsupported. A target that used VEH must restart before another attach. Read activeInterface because Cheat Engine can fall back.

interface.description: default, windows, veh or kernel. default follows the debugger interface selected in Cheat Engine's settings, needs the same exposure switch as that interface and is refused for the DBVM debugger.

attached.description: Whether Cheat Engine reports a debugger attached.

alreadyAttached.description: Whether the requested interface was already attached.

requestedInterface.description: The interface requested by the caller.

activeInterface.description: The interface Cheat Engine actually activated.

usedFallback.description: Whether Cheat Engine selected a different interface than the explicit request.

debugger_break_thread.name: debugger_break_thread
debugger_break_thread.title: Break a thread
debugger_break_thread.description: Requests that one target thread break. The call only submits the request; poll debugger_get_status for the stopped context.

threadId.description: The positive target thread identifier from process_list_threads.
The target thread identifier supplied by the caller.

requested.description: Whether Cheat Engine accepted the break request; poll debugger_get_status for the stop.

debugger_continue.name: debugger_continue
debugger_continue.title: Continue debugger
debugger_continue.description: Continues the current stopped debugger context. The target remains stopped when no broken context exists.

continued.description: Whether Cheat Engine accepted the continuation request.

debugger_delete_breakpoint.name: debugger_delete_breakpoint
debugger_delete_breakpoint.title: Delete debugger breakpoint
debugger_delete_breakpoint.description: Releases an MCP-owned breakpoint at address. It refuses when the address belongs only to a breakpoint created by Cheat Engine or another owner, preserving user breakpoints. Cleanup failure is reported as partial_effect.

address.description: The address expression of an MCP-owned breakpoint.
The breakpoint address supplied by the caller.

released.description: Whether Cheat Engine confirmed removal of the owned breakpoint.

cleanupError.description: A bounded cleanup error when removal could not be confirmed.

debugger_detach.name: debugger_detach
debugger_detach.title: Detach debugger
debugger_detach.description: Resumes a stopped debugger context, unpauses the selected target and detaches Cheat Engine's debugger. Refuses with busy while any resource this MCP activation tracks still holds target state, whatever its kind (breakpoint, debugger or other job, pause, allocation, patch, scan, speedhack and so on); release it first. Cheat Engine's Lua state is re-read before deciding, so jobs and breakpoints that already ended there, for example at their TTL, no longer block.

processId.description: The selected target process identifier when detachment ran.

wasAttached.description: Whether Cheat Engine reported an attached debugger before the call.

continued.description: Whether a broken debugger context was resumed before detaching.

detached.description: Whether Cheat Engine reports the debugger detached after the call.

debugger_get_context.name: debugger_get_context
debugger_get_context.title: Get debugger context
debugger_get_context.description: Copies normalised registers from the current stopped context; integer registers are uppercase hexadecimal without 0x. Include extra registers only when FPU or XMM values matter: Cheat Engine then supplies FP0-FP7 (10 bytes each) and XMM0-XMM15 (16 bytes each; XMM0-XMM7 on 32-bit targets) as byte arrays, returned as space-separated hexadecimal bytes in memory order, least significant byte first.

includeExtraRegisters.description: Include the FPU (FP0-FP7) and XMM registers where Cheat Engine exposes them, as space-separated hexadecimal bytes.

is64Bit.description: Whether the target is 64-bit according to Cheat Engine.

registers.description: Uppercase register names mapped to text: integer registers as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x; byte-array registers such as FP0-FP7 and XMM0-XMM15 as space-separated hexadecimal bytes in memory order, least significant byte first; any other value as bounded text.

includesExtraRegisters.description: Whether FPU and XMM registers were requested; they appear in registers only where Cheat Engine supplied them.

debugger_get_status.name: debugger_get_status
debugger_get_status.title: Get debugger status
debugger_get_status.description: Reads Cheat Engine's debugger state. broken is proven by obtaining the context and is more reliable than reportedBroken alone. Poll after debugger_break_thread because a break request is asynchronous.

stateValid.description: Whether Cheat Engine returned a complete debugger-state snapshot.

canBreak.description: Whether Cheat Engine currently permits a break request.

broken.description: Whether debug_getContext proved that a broken context is available.

reportedBroken.description: The separate state reported by debug_isBroken.

stepping.description: Whether Cheat Engine reports that it is single stepping.

activeInterface.description: The active debugger interface when attached.

error.description: A bounded host message when the state could not be read.

debugger_list_breakpoints.name: debugger_list_breakpoints
debugger_list_breakpoints.title: List debugger breakpoints
debugger_list_breakpoints.description: Copies up to 1024 breakpoint addresses from Cheat Engine and identifies entries this MCP activation owns.

limit.description: The maximum addresses to copy, from 1 through 1024.

breakpoints.description: The breakpoint addresses copied from Cheat Engine.

address.description: The breakpoint address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

owned.description: Whether this activation owns a removable resource at the address.

resourceId.description: The MCP resource id when owned is true.

total.description: The number Cheat Engine reported before the response limit.

truncated.description: Whether the response omitted remaining breakpoints.

debugger_run_to.name: debugger_run_to
debugger_run_to.title: Run debugger to address
debugger_run_to.description: Arms a TTL-bounded one-shot execute breakpoint and continues the current stopped thread. On hit the breakpoint removes itself and the thread remains stopped. Runtime jobs track and release the still-armed breakpoint.

address.description: The destination instruction address expression.

lifetimeSeconds.description: The job lifetime in seconds. Defaults to the configured job TTL and is at most 300 seconds.

jobId.description: The job identifier; runtime_list_jobs reports whether the target reached it.

processId.description: The target process identifier captured at start.

address.description: The destination instruction address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

lifetimeSeconds.description: How long the one-shot breakpoint remains armed, in seconds.

debugger_set_breakpoint.name: debugger_set_breakpoint
debugger_set_breakpoint.title: Set debugger breakpoint
debugger_set_breakpoint.description: Creates a tracked execute, access or write breakpoint. Hardware slots are scarce; data watches require an aligned size of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes, and eight-byte watches require x64. MCP records only its own breakpoint so debugger_delete_breakpoint never removes one created in Cheat Engine's UI.

address.description: A bounded Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C0.

size.description: The watched byte count: 1, 2, 4 or 8. Execute ignores it.

threadId.description: Restrict the breakpoint to this target thread; omit for all threads.

oneShot.description: Remove the breakpoint after its first hit while leaving the thread stopped.

resourceId.description: The resource identifier used by runtime_list_resources and debugger_delete_breakpoint.

address.description: The resolved breakpoint address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The watched byte count. Execute breakpoints ignore it.

threadId.description: Whether the breakpoint is restricted to one target thread.

oneShot.description: Whether the breakpoint removes itself when it fires.

debugger_set_register.name: debugger_set_register
debugger_set_register.title: Set debugger register
debugger_set_register.description: Writes a general-purpose register or EFLAGS in the current stopped context, then reads it back. Changing RIP redirects execution, so use a verified instruction boundary.

register.description: A supported general-purpose register or EFLAGS.

value.description: The signed integer value to write. Use -1 for an all-ones unsigned register value.

contextRegister.description: The concrete context register Cheat Engine wrote.

value.description: The verified register value, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

verified.description: Whether a fresh context read matched the requested value.

debugger_start_capture.name: debugger_start_capture
debugger_start_capture.title: Start debugger capture
debugger_start_capture.description: Starts a TTL-bounded access, write or execute capture. The callback records bounded contexts and automatically continues the target. With groupByEffectiveAddress, an execute capture groups hits by the memory address that the instruction's operand accesses, like Cheat Engine's find out what addresses this instruction accesses. Poll with debugger_poll_capture and stop or release the returned job with runtime_stop_job.

address.description: The address expression to capture.

size.description: The watched byte count: 1, 2, 4 or 8. Execute ignores it.

aggregateByInstruction.description: Group repeated hits by instruction address and retain first and last contexts.

groupByEffectiveAddress.description: Group repeated hits by the effective address of the instruction's one [...] memory operand, computed from the registers before it runs, and report effectiveAddress and operandSize per group with first and last contexts. Needs trigger execute on that instruction and excludes aggregateByInstruction. lea and nop, instructions without exactly one memory operand, fs: or gs: operands, vector-indexed operands and 16-bit addressing are refused before any breakpoint is set.

maximumHits.description: The maximum retained hits, instruction groups or effective-address groups, from 1 through 1024 and the configured job buffer limit.

lifetimeSeconds.description: The job lifetime in seconds. Defaults to the configured job TTL and is at most 300 seconds.

jobId.description: The job identifier; poll it or stop it with runtime_stop_job.

processId.description: The target process identifier captured at start.

address.description: The resolved breakpoint address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

lifetimeSeconds.description: How long the job and its results remain available, in seconds.

debugger_start_trace.name: debugger_start_trace
debugger_start_trace.title: Start debugger trace
debugger_start_trace.description: Arms an execute breakpoint and then traces only the hitting thread for at most 256 steps. Only one trace can run at a time, because it installs Cheat Engine's global debugger_onBreakpoint hook while active: the call refuses (host_refused) while any debugger_onBreakpoint hook is installed, such as another trace or one set with lua_execute, and the job fails if one appears before its entry breakpoint is hit. The trace completes after maximumSteps contexts, the entry context included, or earlier after the first context that matches stopCondition. Completion leaves the thread stopped; runtime_stop_job releases the job and its hook.

address.description: The instruction address expression where the trace starts.

mode.description: into follows calls; over steps across them.

maximumSteps.description: The contexts to retain and execute, from 1 through 256, the entry context included; without stopCondition the trace runs all of them.

stopCondition.description: An optional equality condition such as RAX=1A or IP=7FF612341000, compared as a hexadecimal number (leading zeros and 0x ignored). It stops the trace after the first matching context, the entry context included. Name a register of the target's width: RAX-R15 and RIP on x64, EAX-EIP on x86, EFLAGS or IP.

includeStack.description: Include the stack pointer in each retained context.

lifetimeSeconds.description: The job lifetime in seconds. Defaults to the configured job TTL and is at most 300 seconds.

jobId.description: The job identifier; poll it or stop it with runtime_stop_job.

processId.description: The target process identifier captured at start.

address.description: The resolved breakpoint address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

lifetimeSeconds.description: How long the job and its results remain available, in seconds.

debugger_step.name: debugger_step
debugger_step.title: Step debugger
debugger_step.description: Steps into or over one instruction from the current stopped context.

mode.description: into follows a call; over runs a call to its return.

continued.description: Whether Cheat Engine accepted the continuation request.

instance_list.name: instance_list
instance_list.title: List Cheat Engine instances
instance_list.description: Lists the local Cheat Engine instances whose MCP plugin is enabled and verified. Call it first: every other tool needs one returned instanceId, and there is no default instance. Names may repeat; route by instanceId. An instanceId changes whenever the plugin is enabled again or CE restarts.

instances.description: The instances whose backend confirmed its registry identity, ordered by name.

instanceId.description: The id to pass as instanceId to every other tool; new on every plugin enable.

name.description: The display name; names may repeat across instances.

processId.description: The Cheat Engine process id, not the target's.

pluginVersion.description: The plugin version of this activation.

discoveryIncomplete.description: True when discovery stopped at its 10 s budget; call instance_list again before concluding that an instance is missing.

lua_execute.name: lua_execute
lua_execute.title: Execute Lua
lua_execute.description: Execute caller-authored Lua through Cheat Engine's unsafe Lua capability. source is compiled as text and runs synchronously on Cheat Engine's main thread, so it can freeze Cheat Engine, change the target or host, access files and network, create state that MCP cannot track, or show a dialog that waits for a person. Returned values are copied with bounds: functions, userdata and CE objects are dropped. Use a dedicated tool whenever one exists; this tool requires Mcp:EnableUnsafeLua.

source.description: Lua 5.3 source, up to 1048576 UTF-8 bytes. It runs with Cheat Engine's full Lua API.

chunkName.description: An optional non-empty Lua chunk name for diagnostics, up to 256 UTF-8 bytes.

ok.description: Whether Lua compiled and completed without raising an error.

phase.description: compile or runtime when Ok is false.

error.description: The Lua compiler or runtime message when Ok is false.

hostEffect.description: The confirmed effect of the caller chunk: completed on success, not_applied after a compile error, or unknown after a runtime error.

returnValues.description: Every returned Lua value in order; opaque values are represented as null or omitted from objects.

droppedOpaqueCount.description: Functions, userdata and threads omitted while copying returned values.

memory_read.name: memory_read
memory_read.title: Read memory
memory_read.description: Read target memory at one address: one typed value, up to 1024 consecutive values of a fixed-size type (count), a string (length) or raw bytes (size). Values are text: decimal integers, round-trippable floats, hexadecimal pointers, spaced hexadecimal bytes. An unreadable address fails with memory_read_failed.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C, [game.exe+10]+8 or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

count.description: How many consecutive values of a fixed-size type to read, 1 to 1024; only 1 for string, wstring and bytes.

size.description: The byte count for valueType bytes, 1 to 16384; refused for other types.

length.description: The maximum string length for string and wstring, 1 to 4096 (default 256); refused for other types.

byteOrder.description: The byte order of the value in memory: little_endian (default) or big_endian, as in emulated GameCube, Wii, Wii U or PS3 memory; big_endian applies only to int16, uint16, int32, uint32, int64, uint64, float and double.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

valueType.description: The value type that was read.

value.description: The value as text when count is 1: decimal integers, round-trippable floats, a hexadecimal pointer, the text of a string or spaced hexadecimal bytes.

values.description: The consecutive values in address order when count is above 1.

memory_read_batch.name: memory_read_batch
memory_read_batch.title: Read many addresses
memory_read_batch.description: Read up to 1024 addresses, each with its own value type, in one call (256 KiB in total). Fixed-size types are read in typed batches; an address that does not resolve or cannot be read reports its own error in band while the others are still read, so check every item.

items.description: The addresses to read, 1 to 1024, each with its value type and, for bytes or strings, its size or length.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

size.description: The byte count, 1 to 16384; required for bytes and refused for other types.

length.description: The maximum string length, 1 to 4096 (default 256); only for string and wstring.

byteOrder.description: The byte order of the value in memory: little_endian (default) or big_endian, as in emulated GameCube, Wii, Wii U or PS3 memory; big_endian applies only to int16, uint16, int32, uint32, int64, uint64, float and double.

failed.description: How many items carry an error instead of a value; check every item.

items.description: One entry per request item, in request order.

address.description: The resolved address in uppercase hexadecimal, or the request text when it did not resolve.

value.description: The value as text, when it was read.

error.description: Why this item was not read; the other items are unaffected.

kind.description: The failure class, such as memory_read_failed or not_found.

memory_write.name: memory_write
memory_write.title: Write memory
memory_write.description: Write one typed value, a string or bytes to target memory. The first 64 bytes of the range are read first and returned as previous, so the write can be undone with valueType bytes; with verify the written bytes are read back. A wrong write can crash the target: write only addresses you identified, one at a time.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

value.description: The value as text: decimal or 0x hexadecimal integers, invariant floats (NaN, Infinity), a hexadecimal pointer, the text of a string or spaced hexadecimal bytes such as 90 90.

repeat.description: How many times to write the bytes back to back, 1 to 65536 (1 MiB in total); only for bytes.

nullTerminate.description: Whether to append a terminating zero character; only for string and wstring.

verify.description: Whether to read the range back and compare it with the written bytes.

byteOrder.description: The byte order of the value in memory: little_endian (default) or big_endian, as in emulated GameCube, Wii, Wii U or PS3 memory; big_endian applies only to int16, uint16, int32, uint32, int64, uint64, float and double.

address.description: The resolved address, uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

previous.description: The first bytes the range held before the write, at most 64, as spaced hexadecimal; write them back with valueType bytes to undo.

verified.description: Whether a read-back matched every written byte; false when verify was off or another writer changed the range.

memory_write_batch.name: memory_write_batch
memory_write_batch.title: Write many addresses
memory_write_batch.description: Write up to 1024 addresses in request order, each with its own value type (1 MiB in total). Every address is resolved before the first write. The writes are not atomic: a failure stops the batch and reports partial_effect with completed, failedIndex and effectState, and the completed items stay written.

items.description: The writes, 1 to 1024, each with its address, value type and value.

address.description: An address or Cheat Engine address expression, such as game.exe+1C or 7FF6A1B2C3D0.

value.description: The value as text: decimal or 0x hexadecimal integers, invariant floats, a hexadecimal pointer, the text of a string or spaced hexadecimal bytes.

byteOrder.description: The byte order of the value in memory: little_endian (default) or big_endian, as in emulated GameCube, Wii, Wii U or PS3 memory; big_endian applies only to int16, uint16, int32, uint32, int64, uint64, float and double.

verify.description: Whether to read every item back after the batch and list the items that differ.

written.description: How many items were written, all of them on success.

verified.description: Whether a read-back matched every item; false when verify was off or an item differs.

mismatched.description: The indices of the items whose read-back differs from the written bytes.

module_get.name: module_get
module_get.title: Get module details
module_get.description: Read one module of the attached process: base, size, file path, its sections (with executable and writable flags) and the fields of its mapped PE header: machine, COFF time stamp, entry point, subsystem, DLL and .NET flags and the PDB it names. The time stamp identifies the build, so keep it to tell later whether the game was updated. module is a name such as game.exe (case-insensitive) or any address expression inside the module.

module.description: The module name, such as game.exe, or an address expression inside it, such as game.exe+1000.

base.description: The base address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

path.description: The module's file on disk, as Cheat Engine reports it.

sections.description: The module's sections, as Cheat Engine enumerates them.

address.description: The section address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

fileOffset.description: The section's offset in the module file, as uppercase hexadecimal.

executable.description: Whether the PE header marks the section as code or executable; omitted when unknown.

writable.description: Whether the PE header marks the section writable; omitted when unknown.

size.description: The mapped size in bytes, when Cheat Engine reports it.

pe.description: The PE header fields; omitted when the mapped header cannot be read or parsed.

machine.description: The CPU the image targets: x86, x64, arm, arm64 or unknown.

timeDateStamp.description: The raw COFF time stamp as uppercase hexadecimal; it identifies a build, and reproducible builds store a hash in it.

headerImageBase.description: The ImageBase field of the mapped header; Windows usually rewrites it to the load address, so it is not the file's preferred base.

subsystem.description: The subsystem, such as windows_gui or windows_cui.

isDll.description: Whether the image is a DLL.

managed.description: Whether the image has a CLR header, which marks a .NET assembly.

timeDateStampUtc.description: The time stamp read as seconds since 1970 in UTC; omitted when it is zero.

entryPoint.description: The entry point address as uppercase hexadecimal; omitted when the image has none.

pdb.description: The PDB the image names in its CodeView record; omitted when it names none.

path.description: The PDB path recorded at link time.

signature.description: The PDB signature GUID, uppercase with dashes.

age.description: The PDB age; a symbol server keys the PDB by GUID and age.

module_list.name: module_list
module_list.title: List modules
module_list.description: Page the modules (EXE and DLLs) loaded in the attached process, or in another process by processId, in Cheat Engine's order. concise returns name, base and size; detailed adds is64Bit and the file path. Filter with nameContains, then page with offset and limit (at most 1000). Use it to classify the runtime (mono, GameAssembly, coreclr) and to find a module for module_get.

processId.description: Another process's id; omit it for the attached process.

nameContains.description: A case-insensitive substring of the module name, such as mono or .dll; at most 256 characters.

offset.description: The index of the first module to return.

limit.description: The most modules to return, 1 to 1000.

format.description: concise (name, base, size) or detailed (adds is64Bit and path).

processId.description: The process whose modules are listed.

total.description: The number of modules that match nameContains.

modules.description: The modules of this page, in Cheat Engine's order.

name.description: The module name, such as game.exe.

base.description: The base address as uppercase hexadecimal without 0x.

size.description: The mapped size in bytes, when Cheat Engine reports it.

is64Bit.description: Whether the module is 64-bit; only with format detailed.

path.description: The module's file on disk; only with format detailed.

nextOffset.description: The offset of the next page; omitted on the last page.

runtime_get_info.name: runtime_get_info
runtime_get_info.title: Get runtime information
runtime_get_info.description: Read the active Client epoch, host version, plugin identity, capability evidence and the Mcp:Enable* gates (gates: autoAssembler, unsafeLua, targetCodeExecution, kernelAccess) before using optional features; a tool whose gate is off is refused with capability_disabled.

epoch.description: The Client runtime epoch. It changes when the host runtime is replaced.

hostVersion.description: The connected Cheat Engine host version.

pluginVersion.description: The plugin assembly version, when available.

pluginFileName.description: The loaded plugin assembly file name, without host directories.

runtimeFileName.description: The runtime file name supplied by the plugin host, without host directories.

capabilities.description: Every Client capability and its evidence.

isAvailable.description: Whether the capability is available to this activation.

reason.description: Why the capability is unavailable, when the host explained it.

evidence.description: The host evidence for the capability state, when present.

gates.description: The Mcp:Enable* switches of this activation, as booleans; runtime_get_info and runtime_get_overview always report them. A tool whose switch is off stays listed but is refused with capability_disabled, and a change applies only after the plugin is disabled and enabled again.

autoAssembler.description: Whether Mcp:EnableAutoAssembler is on: callers may check and apply their own Auto Assembler scripts, including Auto Assembler records. Template generation works either way.

unsafeLua.description: Whether Mcp:EnableUnsafeLua is on: callers may run their own Lua and load tables that carry Lua. Fixed tool Lua works either way; with this switch on, the other switches are advisory.

targetCodeExecution.description: Whether Mcp:EnableTargetCodeExecution is on: tools may run code in the target or in Cheat Engine, such as remote calls, DLL and .NET injection, C and C# compilation, Mono attach and invocation, and the speedhack.

kernelAccess.description: Whether Mcp:EnableKernelAccess is on: tools may use the DBK kernel driver and DBVM for physical memory, control and model-specific registers, and kernel-mode reads and writes.

runtime_get_overview.name: runtime_get_overview
runtime_get_overview.title: Get runtime overview
runtime_get_overview.description: Read the host capability snapshot, the Mcp:Enable* gates (runtime.gates), the current target and the retained resource and job counts before starting target work.

runtime.description: The activation identity, host capability evidence and Mcp:Enable* switches.

epoch.description: The Client runtime epoch. It changes when the host runtime is replaced.

hostVersion.description: The connected Cheat Engine host version.

pluginVersion.description: The plugin assembly version, when available.

pluginFileName.description: The loaded plugin assembly file name, without host directories.

runtimeFileName.description: The runtime file name supplied by the plugin host, without host directories.

capabilities.description: Every Client capability and its evidence.

isAvailable.description: Whether the capability is available to this activation.

reason.description: Why the capability is unavailable, when the host explained it.

evidence.description: The host evidence for the capability state, when present.

gates.description: The Mcp:Enable* switches of this activation, as booleans; runtime_get_info and runtime_get_overview always report them. A tool whose switch is off stays listed but is refused with capability_disabled, and a change applies only after the plugin is disabled and enabled again.

autoAssembler.description: Whether Mcp:EnableAutoAssembler is on: callers may check and apply their own Auto Assembler scripts, including Auto Assembler records. Template generation works either way.

unsafeLua.description: Whether Mcp:EnableUnsafeLua is on: callers may run their own Lua and load tables that carry Lua. Fixed tool Lua works either way; with this switch on, the other switches are advisory.

targetCodeExecution.description: Whether Mcp:EnableTargetCodeExecution is on: tools may run code in the target or in Cheat Engine, such as remote calls, DLL and .NET injection, C and C# compilation, Mono attach and invocation, and the speedhack.

kernelAccess.description: Whether Mcp:EnableKernelAccess is on: tools may use the DBK kernel driver and DBVM for physical memory, control and model-specific registers, and kernel-mode reads and writes.

process.description: The currently selected target, if any.

isOpen.description: Whether Cheat Engine currently has a selected target.

processId.description: The selected process id, when a target is open.

processName.description: The selected process name, when a target is open.

pointerSize.description: The configured target pointer width in bytes, when a target is open.

selectionEpoch.description: The target-selection epoch, when a target is open.

resourceCount.description: Resources that this activation or an earlier activation still reports.

runtime_stop_job.name: runtime_stop_job
runtime_stop_job.title: Stop a job
runtime_stop_job.description: Stop one retained job and discard its items. A managed job may report partial_effect while it is still ending; repeat only when the error says retryable.

jobId.description: The job id returned by a start tool.

released.description: Whether the job and its host state are released.

alreadyReleased.description: Whether the job had already ended or been stopped, so nothing more was done.
